blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — intra-articular corticosteroid use in knee osteoarthritis
stem: A client with knee osteoarthritis asks why corticosteroid injections into the same joint are not scheduled on a frequent routine basis. Which response by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: Intra-articular corticosteroids can provide short-term symptom relief, but repeated exposure has potential joint harms, including concern for accelerated osteoarthritis, so repeat timing is individualized.
options.B: Intra-articular corticosteroids do not improve knee osteoarthritis pain or function, so repeating an injection has no therapeutic role for any symptomatic client.
options.C: Intra-articular corticosteroids require daily joint injections to maintain their effect, and missing a planned daily dose commonly causes rebound inflammatory arthritis.
options.D: Intra-articular corticosteroids are considered free of cumulative local joint risk, so frequent repeat injections can be scheduled without regard to prior response or joint status.

rationale: The current AAOS knee osteoarthritis guideline states that intra-articular corticosteroids can provide short-term relief and notes that the recommendation was downgraded because of potential risk of accelerating osteoarthritis from injections. Repeat injection decisions therefore require clinical judgment rather than an unlimited routine schedule. B denies a supported short-term benefit, C invents a daily dosing model, and D contradicts the recognized potential joint harm. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Explain that intra-articular corticosteroids may provide short-term knee osteoarthritis relief while repeat injection timing remains individualized because potential joint harms must be considered.
source_document_title: Management of Osteoarthritis of the Knee (Non-Arthroplasty), Third Edition — Clinical Practice Guideline
source_version_date: Published August 31, 2021 and still listed by AAOS as the current knee osteoarthritis non-arthroplasty CPG in 2026; accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: Intra-Articular Corticosteroids recommendation: may provide short-term relief; rationale notes effect up to about 3 months and recommendation downgrade because of potential risk in accelerating osteoarthritis from injections.
source_claim_supported: AAOS supports short-term symptomatic benefit from intra-articular corticosteroids while recognizing potential risk of accelerated osteoarthritis, supporting individualized rather than unlimited frequent repeat use.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: educate clients about medications, evaluate response, and recognize medication-related adverse effects.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Removed absolute-word cueing and rewrote all options as complete statements of comparable length.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches the current AAOS knee OA CPG; no second answer or residual absolute-word cue remains.
